cards.text: David is king, and a delivery shows up from Hiram, king of Tyre. Envoys, cedar logs, stonemasons AND carpenters. Friend, that's not a gift basket. That's a whole construction crew.

cards.question: Hiram's stonemasons and carpenters roll in with cedar logs. What did Hiram send them to build for David?

cards.text: With cedar logs piling up outside his door, something finally clicks for David.

cards.question: David realizes the ___ has made him king over Israel and lifted his kingdom high for the sake of His ___.

cards.text: In Jerusalem, David takes more wives and has more sons and daughters, and the list of kids born there runs thirteen names long, Solomon included. THIRTEEN. I had six cookie cutters on one counter and thought that was a crowded kitchen.
The Philistines hear David's been anointed king over all Israel, and they all go out searching for him. And trust me, friend, these folks are NOT bringing cedar logs.

cards.question: David learns the Philistines are searching for him, so he hides until they give up and go home.

cards.text: The Philistines come and raid the Valley of Rephaim. But before David makes a single move, there's something he does first.

cards.question: The Philistines are raiding the Valley of Rephaim. What does David do before he goes up against them?

answers.text: He asks God what to do
He sends gifts to make peace

cards.question: When David asks, the LORD tells him to go and promises to deliver the Philistines into his hand.

cards.text: So David and his men go up to Baal-perazim, and David defeats the Philistines. Just like God said. JUST like He said.

cards.question: After the win at Baal-perazim, David gives the credit to the courage of his men.

cards.text: David says, “Like a bursting flood, God has burst out against my enemies by my hand.” Then the Philistines run so fast they leave something behind, something they should NEVER leave behind.

cards.question: The Philistines flee Baal-perazim and leave something behind. What do they abandon there?
The Philistines left their gods behind at Baal-perazim. What does David order done with them?

cards.text: But the Philistines aren't done. Once again, they raid the valley. It's the snooze button all over again: you KNOW it's coming back.

cards.question: With the Philistines back in the valley, David skips asking God this time, since he already won once.

cards.text: David asks God again, and God answers. But this time, the plan is different.

cards.question: God gives David a new plan for the second Philistine raid. What is it?

answers.text: Circle around to the balsam trees
Wait for them back in Jerusalem

cards.text: Then God gives David a signal, up in the tops of the balsam trees. The second he hears it, he moves out to battle.

cards.question: David's signal to move out is the sound of ___ in the tops of the balsam trees.
When David hears marching in the tops of the balsam trees, what does God say it will mean?

answers.text: God has gone out ahead of him
His army is ready to fight

cards.text: So David does exactly as God commanded him. Friend, when the signal is coming from the TREETOPS, you do not freestyle.

cards.question: Following God's plan, David's men strike down the Philistine army all the way from ___ to ___.

cards.text: And after all that, David's fame goes out into every land. Every. Single. One.

cards.question: As David's fame spreads, all the nations come to fear him. Who causes that?

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: "David is king, and a delivery shows up from Hiram, king of Tyre." / "Envoys, cedar logs, stonemasons AND carpenters." / "Friend, that's not a gift basket." / "That's a whole construction crew." The limit is three.

rule.text: **The opening card** can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: "With cedar logs piling up outside his door, something finally clicks for David" makes Hiram's gift the cause of David's realization. Verse 2 only says "And David realized," so the text leaves that connection open. "Finally" also adds a delay the text never mentions.

rule.text: **Leave open what the text leaves open:** who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "But before David makes a single move, there's something he does first" says David hasn't acted yet. Verse 8 already says David "went out to face them," so this line says something the text shows is wrong.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "So David and his men go up to Baal-perazim, and David defeats the Philistines." / "Just like God said." / "JUST like He said."

rule.text: **Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.**

findings.problem: "Then the Philistines run so fast they leave something behind" is told as part of the passage, not as a joke. Verse 12 only says the Philistines abandoned their gods. It says nothing about running fast.

rule.text: **Don't stretch the text.** Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "But the Philistines aren't done." / "Once again, they raid the valley." / "It's the snooze button all over again: you KNOW it's coming back."

rule.text: **Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.**
